newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU WARNS TELEFONICA ABOUT ANTENA 3 DEAL.
newsitem.headline: EU WARNS TELEFONICA ABOUT ANTENA 3 DEAL.

text.p: The European Commission warned Spanish telecommunications company Telefonica in a letter on Thursday against proceeding with its purchase of a stake in television station Antena 3 without EU regulatory approval, a Commission spokesman said.
The spokesman said the Commission had not at this stage reached any conclusions about whether the planned acquisition was in breach of European Union fair competition rules.

But it was important to inform Telefonica that the deal had been challenged by CanalSatelite, the Spanish digital television platform backed by Canal Plus of France, before it was confirmed at a meeting on August 18.
"This is a precautionary measure to avoid the irreparable," the spokesman told Reuters.

CanalSatellite and Telefonica, which has also developed a digital pay-TV package called Via Digital, have been embroiled in a bitter dispute for months which has also opposed the conservative government of Jose Maria Aznar against the Socialist Party.

The Commission asked Telefonica to inform the shareholders of Antena 3 and Audiovisual Sport, which has agreed to sell to Via Digital its lucrative rights to broadcast soccer matches, of CanalSatelite's objections by later today, according to the letter made available to Reuters.

Telefonica announced in a recent surprise move that it had agreed to buy 25 percent of Antena 3, formerly a key partner in CanalSatelite's digital platform, and to purchase 49 percent of Gestora de Medios Audiovisuales Futbol, Audiovisual's parent.
Spanish banks Santander and BCH have agreed to increase their participation in Antena 3 to 21.57 percent and 21.36 percent respectively also on August 18.

The transactions do not fall under the EU's merger rules because the companies involved do more than two thirds of their turnover in Spain. But CanalSatelite argued in two recent complaints that Telefonica was abusing its dominant position in breach of articles 85 and 86 of the EU's founding treaty.
The Commission has not yet decided whether those articles are applicable, but its competition division's first reaction is that "something is not right", a Commission source said.
The Commission ban or impose strict conditions to the deals if found to harm competition. There is no deadline for it to give its final ruling.
Telefonica must comment to the Commission about CanalSatelite's complaints by September 1. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
